chunks: My father (rah) said: It was narrated to me by Abdullah ibn Ja'far from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Kulayb al-Saydawi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is written in the Torah that 'My houses on earth are mosques,' so good fortune to him who purifies himself in his house then visits Me, and it is incumbent upon the visited to honor the visitor.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for performing ablution at home and then going to the mosque?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith as a *khabar al-kitab* (report from previous scriptures), linking the Islamic concept of the mosque to the Torah's declaration that God's houses are on earth. It emphasizes the spiritual merit of transitioning from domestic purification to communal worship, framing the believer's visit as a guest-host relationship where God reciprocates the believer's reverence with honor.
